title: Billing Subject Matter Expert- Support
description: Elation Health is deeply committed to helping independent primary care practices take better care of their patients. Since 2010, we've built a clinical-first, collaborative EHR platform — and with the addition of Elation Billing, we're bringing that same clinical-first philosophy to the revenue side of the practice, so billing works with the chart instead of around it. Elation Health is searching for a Support Subject Matter Expert in Elation Billing — someone who has already done real medical billing and revenue cycle management work, not someone learning it on the job. This is a hands-on, case-based role embedded directly in our support queue: you'll bring practitioner-level RCM judgment to the billing cases our Technical Support Specialists can't fully resolve through process or AI-assisted troubleshooting alone, and you'll help the rest of the team get sharper at spotting those cases in the first place. This isn't a back-office consulting role. You'll be working live cases day to day alongside our support team, diagnosing whether an issue is a product bug, a payer-specific quirk, or a mismatch between how a practice actually operates and how they've configured their billing workflow — then resolving it with the kind of judgment that only comes from having sat inside a claims lifecycle before. Responsibilities Serve as the Elation Billing product line's embedded RCM expert, owning complex billing and revenue cycle cases that require practitioner-level judgment — claims lifecycle issues, CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, payer adjudication and denial patterns, A/R and collections workflows. Act as the go-to resource for case swarms and escalations within Elation Billing whenever a Technical Support Specialist's investigation surfaces a billing nuance beyond scripted troubleshooting. Diagnose a practice's underlying billing context — payment model (insurance-taking vs. DPC), staffing structure, and prior workflow choices — to distinguish genuine product issues from configuration or workflow mismatches, rather than treating every case as a symptom in isolation. Partner with Product and Prod Dev, turning recurring billing edge cases, payer-specific patterns, and denial trends into structured feedback that can inform the roadmap. Contribute to and maintain the team's billing-related knowledge base, SOPs, and macros, and help calibrate the AI Case Assistant's billing-related suggestions so resolutions compound across the team rather than living only in your own case history. Help build the broader team's baseline RCM literacy — sharing real-world billing context so Specialists can better anticipate the issues different practice types are prone to. Track and report on billing-case quality and resolution metrics within your scope, and flag systemic patterns rather than resolving the same root cause case-by-case indefinitely. Requirements 3+ years of hands-on medical billing / revenue cycle management experience — claims submission, payer follow-up, denial management, and A/R — brought in from outside a support organization, not built up through support tenure. Working fluency in CPT/ICD-10 coding logic, claims adjudication, and payer-specific billing rules across commercial and government payers. Experience working within an EHR, practice management, or medical billing platform (e.g., Epic, athenahealth, Waystar, or similar). Strong written and verbal communicator, able to translate complex billing and RCM concepts into clear guidance for both practices and internal teams. Comfortable working directly in a live case queue - this is a frontline, hands-on role, not a periodic-consulting one. Self-directed and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know when a case needs to go beyond a scripted answer. Preferred Certification such as CPB (Certified Professional Biller), CRCR (Certified Revenue Cycle Representative), or CHFP (in progress or completed). Prior experience supporting independent primary care or small-group practices specifically. Experience on a support, customer success, or implementation team at a SaaS/EHR company. Exposure to AI-assisted support or case-management tooling. Six Sigma, Lean, or other process-improvement background. In this role, you will have the opportunity to see the full picture: the medications on the kitchen table, the caregiver dynamics, the fall risks, the barriers to follow-up, and the early warning signs that may never surface in a clinic visit. title: Implementation Manager
description: Counterpart: Value-based care, at the point of care. At Counterpart Health, we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant. By supporting Primary Care Physicians (PCPs), we are able to deliver improved outcomes to our patients at a lower cost through early diagnosis and longitudinal care management of chronic conditions. We are hiring an Implementation Manager on the Counterpart Assistant team. In this role, you will lead the customer-facing work of bringing new provider practices and TINs from late-stage prospects through successful launch on Counterpart Assistant. You will partner closely with account management to hand off new customers, own the customer relationship through implementation, and drive each launch to completion on time and at quality. You will independently lead multiple concurrent implementations and the cross-functional work that makes each launch happen. Partnering with account management, support, product, and engineering internally and with providers, office managers, and clinical leads on the customer side: you will drive accountability across every stakeholder and deliver results through influence. Beyond running individual launches, you will help shape the implementation playbook itself — identifying what slows launches down, proposing changes, and driving improvements that reduce time-to-launch and lift customer satisfaction. Strong project management fundamentals, clear customer communication, working knowledge of clinical data, and technical fluency will let you keep complex, multi-stakeholder launches on track. As an Implementation Manager, you will: Own the customer relationship through implementation: you are the primary point of contact for the customer's technical implementation from project kickoff to post go live steady state. Lead end-to-end project plans for multiple concurrent, multi-step implementations, keeping internal and customer teams aligned on scope, timeline, and status. Partner cross-functionally with account management, support, product, and engineering to unblock issues, coordinate handoffs, and keep implementations moving on schedule. Own the outcomes of each implementation: surface risks early, drive resolution across teams, and hold each launch accountable to its target date and quality bar. Apply technical judgment to monitor and address potential integration issues that arise during implementations, working alongside product and engineering to ensure a successful integration and product launch. Drive continuous improvement of the implementation process: define and refine the playbook, tooling, and templates that reduce time-to-launch and raise the quality bar for every customer experience. Represent the customer's voice internally — capture feedback and pain points from implementations and channel them to product, engineering, and support to improve future launches. Success in this Role Looks Like: Over the first 90 days, you hit the ground running: shadowing active implementations, learning the moving parts of the process (standard EHR integrations, internal system configurations and project plans), and taking ownership of your first launch. Within the first 6 months, you are the customer-facing lead on multiple concurrent implementations, delivering launches on time and with a high customer satisfaction bar. Customers describe you as trusted, responsive, and a reason they feel confident in Counterpart. You have identified at least one meaningful improvement to the implementation process — a template, a workflow change, a handoff refinement — and driven it to adoption across the team. Over time, your performance is measured by the consistency, speed, and on-target delivery of customer implementations, by the strength of the relationships you build with customer stakeholders throughout the process, and by the cumulative improvements you drive into the implementation playbook itself. You should get in touch if: You have 5-8 years of experience leading technical product implementations in a customer-facing role, with a strong track record of on-time, high-quality launches — and of running multiple implementations in parallel. You have 2+ years of experience in healthcare technology implementations working with provider practices, ideally including EHR standard integrations. You have exceptional customer-facing skills — you build trust quickly with providers, office managers, and clinical leads, communicate clearly under pressure, and manage escalations calmly and directly. You are an expert in project management: you set the plan, track it, and drive accountability across internal and customer teams that don't report to you. You have strong technical judgment and are comfortable diagnosing potential integration issues and scope creep of the overall project. You are a strong communicator, clearly documenting project status and potential risks internally and externally. You lead through influence, not authority: you know how to align stakeholders, resolve conflict, and hold the room accountable to outcomes. Lead executive business reviews and regular check-ins that drive adoption, surface underused features, and strengthen product alignment. Own renewals and retention. Your success is measured on net dollar retention for your book. Surface expansion opportunities and partner with our expansion team to close them. Bring the voice of the customer inside. Share what you learn with Product and cross-functional teams to help shape the roadmap, onboarding, and how we work. Design your own workflows. You thrive while things are still being built. You’re comfortable shaping processes as we go and don’t need a playbook for everything. You’re excited about how AI can transform your work. You look for ways to reduce manual overhead and spend your time where it matters most. Technical aptitude. You’re comfortable learning and navigating complex software, and you want to become an expert in our product. title: Director, GTM Strategy, Planning & Analytics
description: Articulate is seeking a Director of GTM Strategy, Planning & Analytics to lead and evolve how we translate company strategy into actionable go-to-market plans, measure business performance, govern the data foundations that support decision-making, and align compensation programs to GTM priorities across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Channel. This role leads an integrated function spanning GTM strategy and planning, forecasting and performance management, analytics and insights, GTM data strategy and governance, and compensation strategy and analytics. The Director will own the end-to-end GTM planning system, translating company growth objectives into targets, capacity and resource plans, forecasts, performance frameworks, and operating rhythms. The role will ensure GTM leaders have clear, decision-ready insights into business performance, risks, opportunities, and tradeoffs. The Director will also provide leadership for GTM data strategy and governance, ensuring that the business logic, metric definitions, data standards, and cross-system requirements underlying GTM decision-making are scalable, consistent, and trusted. In partnership with centralized Data, Engineering, IT, and other teams, this role will establish GTM priorities and requirements while those technical organizations retain responsibility for technical architecture and development. As the leader of this function, the Director will define priorities and operating models, develop managers and senior individual contributors, and partner closely with GTM, Finance, Data, IT, and executive stakeholders to operationalize company strategy and improve GTM performance. What you'll do: GTM Strategy, Planning & Operating System Lead the end-to-end GTM planning system, including annual and quarterly planning, forecasting, target setting, capacity planning, resource allocation, and performance management. Translate company growth objectives and strategic priorities into aligned GTM targets, resource plans, and execution strategies across functions, segments, regions, and products. Establish and continuously improve GTM operating rhythms, including planning cycles, forecast reviews, executive business reviews, and performance-management processes. Develop scalable planning frameworks, governance models, and operating standards that enable GTM teams to adapt to changing business priorities. Evaluate strategic tradeoffs across GTM investments and develop recommendations regarding capacity, coverage, demand generation, retention, enablement, and other GTM investments. Partner with Finance and GTM leadership on scenario planning, investment decisions, and resource allocation. Business Performance, Analytics & Insights Define performance measurement frameworks that provide consistent visibility into GTM health across the customer lifecycle. Lead the development of analytics and insights that enable GTM leaders to understand performance, identify risks and opportunities, and make informed business decisions. Ensure forecasting, pipeline, funnel, retention, productivity, and other critical GTM performance measures are clearly defined and consistently understood. Translate complex business performance into clear, decision-ready insights and recommendations. Identify emerging performance trends and develop recommendations to improve near- and medium-term GTM effectiveness. Establish priorities for GTM analytics based on business impact and ensure analytical resources are focused on the highest-value questions. GTM Data Strategy & Governance Lead the GTM data strategy and governance function, establishing priorities for the integrity, scalability, and evolution of the GTM data foundation. Ensure consistent GTM business logic, metric definitions, dimensions, and data standards across systems, reporting, and business processes. Establish governance for GTM data definitions, lineage, quality, and usage in partnership with Data, Engineering, IT, Finance, and GTM stakeholders. Ensure GTM business requirements are clearly defined and aligned before technical development begins. Oversee prioritization of GTM data initiatives and make recommendations regarding sequencing, dependencies, business impact, and tradeoffs. Ensure data structures and governed data assets support critical GTM use cases including forecasting, pipeline management, compensation, retention, planning, and performance measurement. Partner with centralized Data and technical organizations to ensure GTM requirements inform technical roadmaps while maintaining clear accountability between business ownership and technical execution. Improve adoption and understanding of governed data assets, metrics, and BI capabilities across GTM. Compensation Strategy & Analytics Lead GTM compensation strategy and planning in partnership with GTM and Finance leadership. Ensure compensation programs align with company objectives, GTM priorities, targets, quotas, and desired business outcomes. Lead compensation modeling and analytics to evaluate program effectiveness, cost, performance, and behavioral impact. Establish governance and decision frameworks for compensation design and changes. Partner with GTM leadership on quota and incentive strategy and provide recommendations regarding tradeoffs and program design. Ensure compensation planning is integrated with broader capacity, target, resource, and financial planning. Strategic Decision Support & Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as a strategic partner to GTM, Finance, Data, IT, and other functional leaders. Structure complex and ambiguous GTM problems, bringing together business context, data, financial implications, and operational considerations. Develop recommendations regarding GTM priorities, investments, organizational tradeoffs, and performance improvement. Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives from problem definition through recommendation and implementation. Collaborate with senior leaders to turn company strategy into actionable GTM plans and ensure alignment across functions. Communicate plans, performance, risks, recommendations, and tradeoffs clearly to senior and executive stakeholders. Leadership & Organizational Development Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization spanning strategy, planning, analytics, data strategy, and compensation. Translate functional priorities into clear objectives, execution plans, and measurable outcomes. Coach managers and individual contributors toward outcomes, impact, and increasingly strategic thinking. Establish clear accountability and decision rights across the function. Build cross-functional relationships that enable the team to operate effectively across organizational boundaries. Continuously evolve the team's capabilities, processes, and operating model as business needs change. Create clarity around priorities and ensure the organization remains focused on its highest-impact work. What you should have: 12+ years of experience in GTM strategy, business operations, revenue operations, planning, analytics, data strategy, or related functions, preferably within B2B SaaS. 5+ years of people leadership experience, including experience leading managers and/or senior individual contributors. Proven experience leading GTM planning, forecasting, target setting, capacity planning, and performance management. Strong understanding of GTM analytics, SaaS metrics, customer lifecycle performance, and executive decision support. Experience with GTM data strategy, metric governance, data definitions, and the relationship between business requirements and modern data ecosystems. Experience with compensation strategy, quota planning, incentive design, compensation analytics, or closely related planning disciplines. Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous business problems and translate complex information into actionable recommendations. Strong systems thinking and understanding of dependencies across CRM, data warehouse, BI, planning, and GTM execution environments. Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Data, IT, and other functions. Strong leadership, communication, prioritization, and judgment. Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience. Compensation The pay range for this position is $163,900 to $245,900 for all US locations. This range represents our good faith expectation of what we reasonably expect to pay for this role based on factors including (but not limited to) skills, experience, training, licensure and certifications, education, and other business and organizational needs. This position is bonus-eligible. Articulate also offers a robust suite of benefits — visit the website for a full list. This is a US-based role and can be performed remotely from anywhere within the United States. Occasional travel for company events may be required. Employees must physically reside and work within the US throughout their employment and must immediately notify Articulate of any change of address. The application window for this position is expected to close 90 days from the original posting date. Founded by Adam Schwartz in 2002, Articulate provides creator tools and services that make it simple for enterprises and SMBs to develop, deliver, and analyze online workplace training that’s engaging and effective. Increasingly, organizations must reskill employees for ever-changing remote and hybrid work environments, create learning cultures that attract and retain employees in a tight labor market, and use training to build more equitable, empowering, and engaging workplaces. Articulate helps organizations address these critical business needs with its creator platform for workplace training. Articulate 360—a suite of creator tools for online courses—was named the 7th most-loved product in the world by TrustRadius in 2021. And Rise —an all-in-one online training system that makes online training easy to create, enjoyable to take, and simple to manage—is the first creator platform for SMBs and departments within the enterprise. Articulate has more than 118,000 customers in 170 countries and counts all 100 of the Fortune 100 companies as customers. Named one of Inc. As a human-centered organization, we honor people’s humanity knowing that each person’s unique history, vulnerabilities, and social location inform how we show up with one another. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An overview of this role</strong></p> <p>We're looking for an experienced Sr Manager, Technical Program Management to lead a team of TPMs in our Engineering org. Our R&D PMO is a new team within GitLab Engineering, so this is a great opportunity to help build out a new function and define the future of Program Management at GitLab.<br><br>This individual will be responsible for leading a team of TPMs of varying levels, all working on different areas of the Product. The Sr. Manager, Technical Program Management will work closely with Product and Engineering leadership to ensure that TPMs are assigned to high priority programs and that they are successfully delivering results for customers. In addition to managing a team, this leadership position will also contribute to the long-term operational success of the R&D organization by partnering with leaders to develop new planning cadences and other improvements to our ways of working.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Responsible for directly GitLab team members performing in the role of Technical Program Manager. Lead and mentor a team of Technical Program Managers, including providing regular feedback to foster their growth and ensure their success.</li> <li>Responsible for staffing requirements for the PMO, in partnership with the Director of Technical Program Management and the Product and engineering Leadership groups. Align TPM team resourcing / assignments with the company’s business objectives.</li> <li>Create and maintain program management standards for elements including program documentation, project plans, status reports, post-mortems as well as a team direction north star; work to continuously improve and iterate on these processes.</li> <li>Create and maintain a long-term strategy and vision for the Program Management function, in alignment with broader company goals. Develop and expand upon the job family, CDF, and long-term hiring and growth objectives for the Technical Program Management function.</li> <li>Build strong relationships  with cross-functional stakeholders including Engineering, Product, Security, and GTM teams.</li> <li>Identify and mitigate risks, resolve conflicts, and remove obstacles for the Technical Program Management team to ensure timely program delivery.</li> <li>Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) for programs and team members and hold the team accountable for meeting commitments.</li> <li>Lead strategic planning with direct influence over staffing decisions, project timelines, and planning stakeholders.</li> <li>Demonstrate leadership as expected of Managers across GitLab and Embody our<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/values/#:~:text=values%20at%20GitLab-,CREDIT,other%20by%20assuming%20good%20intent."> CREDIT values</a> in your work</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Prior experience as a people manager and as an IC TPM, ideally in a position of seniority</li> <li>Ability to prioritize and delegate work effectively</li> <li>Proven track record of successful collaboration with internal and external stakeholders</li> <li>Experience developing and executing on strategic team development plans </li> <li>Ability to coach others on driving cross functional product-driven initiatives, without direct control of the programs</li> <li>Proven ability to position oneself and the team as trusted partners and thought leaders</li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/job-families/engineering/technical-program-management/#senior-manager-technical-program-management">More information about the Sr Manager Job Family is available in our handbook</a>.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>Our Technical Program Management function is relatively new to GitLab; title: Growth Marketer, Creators & Channels
description: ABOUT SUPABASE Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. ABOUT THE ROLE Creator and UGC content is only getting bigger as a growth channel for developer tools, and right now Supabase reaches it mostly at arm's length, through agencies that own the actual relationships with creators. This role exists to change that: bring our creator/influencer program fully in-house, own those relationships directly, and grow the program into a multi-million-dollar channel. A good marker of success looks like a roster of around 50 active creators within the first year — at which point we take what worked and go find the next channel to unlock the same way. This is a growth and marketing role first, not a DevRel or engineering-adjacent one — we're optimizing less for technical depth and more for someone outgoing enough that creators want to work with them directly, creative enough to keep testing new formats and strategies, and operationally strong enough to run the budgets and reporting behind it. The work is currently split on an interim basis across a couple of people on the marketing team; this role is being created to own it end to end. WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR - Source, recruit, and manage direct relationships with content creators (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) - Design and run creator campaigns end to end - Find and test new acquisition channels and strategies — lots of small experiments, doubling down on what works - Operationalize and report on these programs: budgets, tracking, results - Grow with the role: the remit could develop into owning all content from a growth perspective, beyond creators and UGC YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU - 3+ years in growth, partnerships or creator marketing at a dev tool, SaaS or consumer tech company - Track record of launching channels from zero — and turning winners into repeatable programs - Outgoing relationship-builder creators genuinely want to work with - Strong operator. Comfortable with spreadsheets. - Ideally already doing a version of this somewhere scrappier or more startup — someone thriving at a smaller company is a better signal here than someone comfortable (but not standout) at a big-name platform WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Corporate Development Director
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2 id="an-overview-of-this-role" data-lfile-container="21ea07e5-ded4-47e8-ad92-4ca7b7d6be35" data-pm-slice="1 1 []">An overview of this role</h2> <p>As the Corporate Development Director, you'll help influence how GitLab invests to win: what we build, what we buy, where we partner, and what we should not pursue. This role sits within the Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships.</p> <p>This role straddles strategy and M&A engagements. You'll lead research that frames GitLab's options: mapping the markets in and around our AI-powered DevSecOps platform, testing where we have a right to win, and turning that into clear recommendations for the executive team. When the answer is to acquire, you'll drive the deal process end to end, from outreach through close and integration.</p> <p>Success here is not measured by deal count. It looks like sharper strategic choices: a well-reasoned point of view on our priority markets, investment theses that product and executive leaders rely on, acquisitions that speed up the roadmap when buying is the right answer, and an educated no when it isn't. You'll own the wider market perspective rather than individual product categories, and work with the team's Analyst on the research behind it.</p> <h2 id="what-youll-do">What you'll do</h2> <h3 id="strategy-and-research">Strategy and research</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Own the wider market view.</strong> Research the broader market GitLab competes in, beyond specific product categories: competitive dynamics, AI-native entrants, technology shifts and where value is moving. Collaborate with the team's Analyst on the research and turn the findings into a clear point of view on where GitLab should play.</li> <li><strong>Build an investment thesis for each focus area.</strong> Work with Product and Engineering leaders to define the problems worth solving, the capabilities GitLab needs, and what it would cost in time and money to get there on our own.</li> <li><strong>Own the competitive and landscape view.</strong> Maintain market maps and a current read on GitLab's competitors: their strategy, product direction, positioning, pricing, and M&A and funding activity. Produce competitor analyses that show where we lead, where we're exposed and how rivals are likely to move. Flag shifts by competitors, hyperscalers and AI labs that change our options, and bring the implications to Product and the executive team.</li> <li><strong>Define where GitLab should not play.</strong> Identify adjacencies that dilute focus and markets where the economics or competition work against us. Make the case for a no with the same rigor as a yes.</li> </ul> <h3 id="build-buy-or-partner">Build, buy or partner</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Run the build, buy, partner analysis.</strong> For each strategic gap, compare the options side by side on speed, cost, risk, control and strategic fit, and bring a clear recommendation.</li> <li><strong>Deliver strategic clarity to</strong> <strong>executives and the Board.</strong> Produce short strategy memos/decks and business cases that set out the decision, the trade-offs and what we give up with each path.</li> <li><strong>Feed company strategy and planning.</strong> Bring an outside-in view of the market and the inorganic options available into annual and long-range planning.</li> <li><strong>Work hand in hand with Strategic Partnerships.</strong> When partnering is the right answer, frame the opportunity and hand it to the partnership owner with a clear thesis. When it isn't, explain why.</li> </ul> <h3 id="deal-execution-and-integration">Deal execution and integration</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Own end-to-end deal process management.</strong> Validate target fit against GitLab's our target profile, product roadmap and other criteria, and build the acquisition rationale and business case. Drive our M&A process from intro call through the various steps through to closing and integration.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate the deal.</strong> Develop valuation, commercial integrity assessment, impact on GitLab's business and provide negotiations assistance to the VP and the executive team.</li> <li><strong>Lead cross-functional diligence.</strong> Run pre-LOI validation and diligence across Product, Engineering, Security, Finance, Legal and People, and communicate findings clearly.</li> <li><strong>Drive deal documents with Legal.</strong> Prepare NDAs, LOIs and purchase agreements with GitLab Legal and outside counsel.</li> <li><strong>Own integration outcomes.</strong> Lead post-acquisition integration as the DRI, measured against the roadmap and business goals in the business case. Bring lessons learned back into the strategy work.</li> <li><strong>Build the external network.</strong> Maintain relationships with founders, executives, investors, bankers and advisors that bring us early insight and pipeline.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-youll-bring">What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Strategy and deal experience.</strong> 8+ years across corporate development, corporate strategy, strategy consulting or technology investing, including 5+ years leading acquisitions end to end in enterprise software.</li> <li><strong>Structured strategic thinking.</strong> You form a point of view from incomplete information, test it against data, and change your mind when the evidence says so. You're as comfortable recommending that we stay out of a market as that we enter it.</li> <li><strong>Market research depth.</strong> Skilled in market sizing, competitive analysis and landscape mapping, and in turning research into a recommendation, not a report.</li> <li><strong>Deal craft.</strong> Skilled in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, negotiation and integration planning, with experience across varied consideration structures.</li> <li><strong>Technical fluency.</strong> A working understanding of software development, DevSecOps and the AI landscape, enough to hold substantive conversations with product and engineering leaders about roadmaps and architecture.</li> <li><strong>Clear executive communication.</strong> You write short, decision-ready updates and present trade-offs plainly to executives and the Board, in an async-first environment.</li> <li><strong>Influence without authority.</strong> You build trust across Product, Engineering, Finance and Legal and move decisions forward across functions.</li> <li><strong>Ownership with collaboration.</strong> You own the strategic view and the recommendation, and partner closely with the team's Analyst on research and analysis.</li> <li><strong>Preferred:</strong> familiarity with the DevSecOps, security, AI and open source ecosystems.</li> <li>You value the <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/" target="_blank">all remote</a> lifestyle and share our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/values/" target="_blank">values</a>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="about-the-team">About the team</h2> <p>The Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team helps GitLab decide how to grow beyond what we build on our own. We own inorganic strategy: acquisitions, strategic partnerships with hyperscalers and AI labs, and the research that tells us which to pursue and which to pass on.</p> <p>We work across Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal and the executive group. We set direction and do the detailed work ourselves, with a high degree of ownership and transparency in a fully remote, asynchronous environment.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Head of Field and Partner Marketing
description: Role Description Dropbox is hiring a Head of Field & Partner Marketing to lead our global field and partner marketing organization and drive pipeline growth across our Sales-Led Growth (SLG) business and strategic partner ecosystem. This executive Go-To-Market (GTM) leader will own the regional marketing strategy, account-based execution, mid-to-bottom funnel demand engines, and partner marketing required to scale business-to-business revenue globally. While our PLG team focuses on the frictionless, self-serve transactional customer lifecycle, this leader owns the end-to-end marketing journey for sales-engaged and partner-led motions. This role requires an exceptional strategic operator who can orchestrate targeted account-based marketing (ABM) and regional demand generation alongside localized partner programs—including managing co-marketing initiatives with strategic AI technology ecosystems (ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) and supporting our distribution networks. Partnering closely with regional Sales and Channel leaders, this executive will oversee integrated campaigns, joint partner value propositions, content strategies, and comprehensive PLG to SLG customer lifecycle initiatives. Responsibilities SLG & Partner Pipeline Accountability: Own the strategic vision and performance metrics (creation, coverage, and acceleration) for both direct field pipeline and indirect partner-led business globally. Integrated Demand Generation: Lead the Integrated Marketing team to design and deploy highly optimized mid- and bottom-funnel acquisition campaigns that move prospects effectively through the sales pipeline. Content & Customer Campaigns: Oversee the upstream Campaigns team to deliver compelling content frameworks and high-impact customer marketing initiatives that drive post-sale engagement, adoption, brand advocacy, and net revenue retention (NRR). Partner Alliance & Co-Marketing: Develop and execute high-impact joint marketing programs with strategic AI and productivity ecosystem partners (including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini). Build compelling value propositions that position Dropbox as the core content layer for modern workflows. Distribution & Channel Support: Oversee marketing strategies to and through Dropbox’s distribution networks and cloud marketplaces to support our incremental channel revenue stream. Account-Based Marketing (ABM) Strategy: Build, scale, and institutionalize Dropbox’s ABM framework. Define account selection, tiering, multi-channel orchestration, and tailored campaigns for high-value corporate and mid-market accounts. PLG-to-SLG Monetization: Partner closely with the PLG Digital Marketing and Product teams to identify accounts with high existing self-serve usage, triggering targeted field and partner campaigns to convert them into larger team or corporate agreements. Sales & Partner Architecture Interlock: Establish trusted partnerships with regional Sales VPs and the Alliance organization to align on territory strategies, partner incentives, target account lists, and quarterly outbound cadences. Experiential & Executive Engagement: Oversee the global portfolio of regional field events, proprietary customer advisory boards (CABs), executive roundtable programs, and major industry tech activations. Team Leadership & Org Design: Manage, mentor, and scale a multi-disciplinary, globally distributed team spanning four core functions: Integrated Marketing (mid/bottom funnel demand), Regional Field Marketing , Partner/Channel Marketing , and Campaigns (Content & Customer Marketing). Foster a high-performance culture tied directly to pipeline health and business outcomes. Requirements 10+ years of B2B marketing experience with increasing leadership responsibility spanning field marketing, partner/channel marketing, and demand generation. 5+ years of experience leading, scaling, and managing multi-disciplinary marketing teams, including direct oversight of demand generation, content/creative production, or customer marketing functions. Ecosystem & Tech Alliance Experience: Proven track record of managing joint marketing programs with major technology platforms, SaaS alliances, or AI ecosystems. Sales Alignment: Experience partnering directly with Sales VPs, directors, and external partner leadership in a multi-tiered GTM environment. B2B Funnel Mastery: Deep understanding of multi-month B2B sales cycles, buying committees, account progression, and revenue attribution models. Data-Driven Mindset: Strong analytical orientation with hands-on experience using pipeline metrics, win rates, funnel velocity, and ROI modeling to drive investment decisions. Preferred Qualifications Hybrid GTM Experience: Proven success working within a hybrid B2B model, specifically leveraging product-led metrics (PQLs, active usage) to fuel sales pipelines and partner co-selling. Global Scale: Experience supporting multi-region sales and partner organizations, with a strong ability to balance global consistency with local market nuances. MarTech/SalesTech Fluency: Familiarity with modern business tech stacks (PRM/Partner Relationship Management systems, CRM, MAP, and ABM/intent data platforms). AI & Cloud Market Fluency: Strong understanding of the modern AI landscape, developer tool ecosystems, and cloud productivity paradigms. Executive Presence: Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to confidently command attention and influence internal leadership and external clients/partners. Durable Skills AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technology continue to evolve: Awareness: Understand yourself and others. Judgment: Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations. Adaptability: Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change. Connection: Communicate, collaborate, and build trust. To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog post from our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser. Compensation US Zone 1 $275,400—$372,600 USD US Zone 2 $247,900—$335,300 USD US Zone 3 $220,300—$298,100 USD

title: Director, Product Marketing
description: Who We Are: SmithRx is a rapidly growing, venture-backed Health-Tech company. Our mission is to disrupt the expensive and inefficient Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) sector by building a next-generation drug acquisition platform driven by cutting edge technology, innovative cost saving tools, and best-in-class customer service. With hundreds of thousands of members onboarded since 2016, SmithRx has a solution that is resonating with clients all across the country. We pride ourselves for our mission-driven and collaborative culture that inspires our employees to do their best work. We believe that the U.S healthcare system is in need of transformation, and we come to work each day dedicated to making that change a reality. At our core, we are guided by our company values: Integrity: Our purpose guides our actions and gives us confidence in the path ahead. With unwavering honesty and dependability, we embrace the pressure of challenging the old and exemplify ethical leadership to create the new. Courage: We face continuous challenges with grit and resilience. We embrace the discomfort of the unknown by balancing autonomy with empathy, and ownership with vulnerability. We boldly challenge the status quo to keep moving forward—always. Together: The success of SmithRx reflects the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team. Our shared values bind us together and make us one. When one falls, we all fall; when one rises, we all rise. Job Summary: We are looking for a strategic and visionary Leader of Product Marketing who will be responsible for leading our overall go-to-market strategy, product positioning, and sales enablement efforts. SmithRx isn’t just building another technology platform; we are rebuilding the pharmacy benefits category from the ground up. In this highly cross-functional leadership role, you will define how we communicate the radical value of SmithRx’s platform to brokers, employers, consultants, and members, establishing us as the clear alternative to the broken status quo. You will be responsible for building, mentoring, and scaling a high-performing product marketing team, bringing complex new capabilities to market, and driving greater adoption of our products and services. As we expand our platform capabilities, a critical part of this role will be navigating the narrative around Artificial Intelligence in healthcare. You will lead the charge in educating our market, building trust around our AI-powered features, and demonstrating how these technologies improve outcomes. To be successful in this role, you should demonstrate a strong track record of scaling PMM functions, driving category creation, translating complex and emerging technologies into compelling stories, and partnering closely with executive leadership across Product and Sales. You must be comfortable operating in an unstructured, fast-paced environment and learning as you experiment. What you will do: Guide Category Creation: Positions SmithRx as a radical departure from traditional PBMs. You will shape market perception and educate the industry on a fundamentally new way to approach pharmacy benefits. Own GTM Strategy: Drive the overarching Go-to-Market (GTM) strategy for SmithRx’s platform and new product features, coordinating cross-functional launches across Product, Clinical Programs, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing to ensure successful rollouts. AI Narrative & Trust Building: Develop and execute GTM strategies for our AI-powered products and features, crafting transparent, education-driven messaging that overcomes industry skepticism and builds deep trust with employers, brokers, and members. Team Leadership: Hire, lead, and develop a team of high-performing product marketers. Positioning & Messaging: Work with our content team to establish compelling, differentiated positioning and messaging that clearly articulates SmithRx's unique value proposition against legacy PBMs for different segments of our target audience (brokers, HR leaders, members, and clinical partners). Sales Enablement: Develop high-impact sales enablement programs and product documentation (pitch decks, case studies, battlecards, solution handbooks) that empower our Sales and Client Success teams to win and retain business. Strategic Measurement: Set measurable and realistic product marketing goals, monitor the progress of GTM initiatives, identify areas for improvement, and compile reports on campaign performance and product adoption for senior management. Voice of Market & Customer: Conduct primary and secondary research to deeply understand the pain points of our buyers and end-users, using these insights to influence the product roadmap and prioritize feature development. Competitive Intelligence: Oversee competitor analysis to understand the strengths and weaknesses of our competitors and identify gaps in their strategies that we can capitalize on. Co-Marketing & Growth: Partner with Growth and Brand Marketing Teams to develop campaign narratives, establish partnerships, and execute co-marketing campaigns that drive pipeline and increase brand awareness. What you will bring to SmithRx: 10+ years of experience in product marketing, with at least 4+ years in a leadership/management role building and scaling PMM teams for B2B or B2B2C technology companies. Bachelor's degree in marketing, business development, or similar (MBA preferred). Category Creation Experience: Proven experience at a disruptive company that fundamentally changed the face of a category. description: Who we are Yubo is the instantly social, social app: the leading real-time social discovery platform where you can meet new people for friendship, crushes and community. Our mission is to help young adults find community - whoever they are, wherever they are and whenever they feel social. That's why we’re building a more spontaneous and human social world, one based on interaction, exploration and possibility. We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow. Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education. We also work closely with the broader technology industry to share our knowledge and NGOs create industry-leading child protection standards. Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions! About this role We are looking for a Senior Marketing Manager to turn Yubo's brand ambition into brilliant, effective marketing, from major campaign moments to paid and owned-channel activity, and the smaller tests that help us learn what works. Reporting to the Director of Brand & Communications, you will translate Yubo's brand strategy into an executable US marketing programme. You will lead integrated brand campaigns, own campaign and paid-media planning and management, and build and manage influencer capabilities. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who can move comfortably between strategic thinking and execution. You will challenge plans constructively, make recommendations grounded in insight and data, and work closely with Creative, PR, Product, UA, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal to deliver marketing that builds the brand and drives growth. The role will focus on the US first, with scope to contribute to expansion into new markets as Yubo's marketing activity grows. This is a freelance position on a 6-month contract, with a target start of Q4 2026. Your responsibilites Turn strategic priorities into impactful marketing activity Lead the development and execution of Yubo's priority brand campaigns in the US, from insight and strategy through briefing, delivery, optimisation and reporting. Translate Yubo's positioning, audience priorities and seasonal moments into cultural marketing activity that earns attention amongst Gen Z. Develop integrated channel plans across paid, earned and owned activity, working closely with PR and Creative to ensure every channel plays a clear role. Own campaign budget planning and day-to-day management, partnering closely with UA on paid-media strategy and optimisation. Explore new, less traditional ways for Yubo to reach and engage people, challenging default channel choices and designing approaches that make marketing work harder. Establish brand marketing operations and measurement Establish effective working rhythms across Brand, Creative, PR, Product, UA and Data, from briefing and approvals to reporting and learning. Work closely with Data and UA to analyse performance and make clear, evidence-based optimisation recommendations. Build clear measurement plans so every campaign, test and experiment informs future investment and potential expansion into new markets. Identify, recommend and deliver smaller tests and experiments that help Yubo learn quickly and improve future investment. Manage influencer agency relationships, negotiating cost-effective partnership models that maximise impact and effectiveness. You know how to turn a positioning and a business objective into a campaign people notice, and how to turn campaign results into smarter decisions next time. You are as comfortable building a strategic recommendation as you are writing a brief, reviewing creative, shaping a media plan, interrogating performance data or getting into the practical detail needed to make work happen. Experience owning campaign and paid-media planning and management, ideally in close partnership with performance marketing, creative and comms teams. Confidence analysing campaign performance and translating data into clear optimisation and investment recommendations. Experience working closely with creative teams to develop strong campaign platforms, briefs and work that is both strategically sharp and creatively ambitious. A curiosity for less traditional channels, partnerships and approaches, with the creativity to test new ways of reaching people and maximise earned attention above what we buy. Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. What we offer Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. The team works in its own environment, separate from the main org, and is agent-first with fast CI, so ideas reach users within a day or two. You’ll own features end to end, from spotting the problem to shipping the product and the backend behind it. Most of what you build is new, in a space where few companies are working with AI and music, so there’s no playbook. You’ll define the problem yourself, test ideas with real users, and work alongside research engineering to turn model capabilities into things people love using. What you ship goes live to a large audience within days. You’re a builder with strong product taste who understands every layer of the system. You use AI to move fast, but you own and understand everything you ship. You care about music and the people who make it. title: Engineering Director, EU
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. We're now entering the next phase of our journey: building and scaling a multi-market European bank.</p> <p>The EU Engineering organisation sits at the centre of that ambition. We are responsible for helping Monzo launch, grow and operate across Europe, navigating everything from product-market fit and customer growth to regulatory requirements, localisation and operational scale.</p> <p>Unlike most engineering organisations at Monzo, EU does not own a single product area. We work horizontally across the company, partnering with teams across Payments, Core Banking, Growth, Wealth, Customer Operations, Fincrime, Platform and many others to bring Monzo's products to new markets and deliver great customer experiences locally.</p> <p>As an Engineering Director, you'll lead a distributed engineering organisation across the UK, Spain and remote locations. You'll partner closely with Product, Design, Data, Operations, Risk, Compliance and executive stakeholders to solve complex problems that span organisational boundaries.</p> <p>Success in this role comes through influence, relationships and organisational leadership as much as execution. You'll need to build alignment across a wide range of teams, create clarity in ambiguity, and help Monzo discover what works in new markets while establishing the foundations that allow us to scale across Europe.</p> <p>This is one of Monzo's most strategically important areas and a unique opportunity to help build a European bank from the ground up.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll work on</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead a distributed engineering organisation spanning multiple squads, markets and countries.</li> <li>Build and develop Engineering Managers, Senior Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders.</li> <li>Partner with Product, Design, Data, Research, Operations, Risk and Compliance leaders to define and execute Monzo's European strategy.</li> <li>Drive alignment and execution across numerous collectives to ensure Europe receives the capabilities it needs to succeed.</li> <li>Shape how Monzo approaches market expansion, localisation, regulatory requirements and multi-market product development.</li> <li>Influence priorities and outcomes across teams that do not directly report to you.</li> <li>Create clarity and momentum in highly ambiguous problem spaces where ownership and solutions are not always obvious.</li> <li>Design and evolve organisational structures, operating models and planning processes that allow Monzo to scale effectively across Europe.</li> <li>Help identify and validate product-market fit in new markets while balancing short-term delivery and long-term strategic investments.</li> <li>Partner closely with executive leadership to shape the future of Monzo's European business.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>You should apply if</strong></h3> <ul> <li>You have experience leading large engineering organisations through other leaders, including Engineering Managers, Senior Engineering Managers and senior individual contributors.</li> <li>You have successfully operated in highly complex organisations where outcomes depend on collaboration across many teams and functions.</li> <li>You are exceptional at building relationships and influencing without direct authority.</li> <li>You can navigate ambiguity and create clarity where goals, ownership or priorities are not yet fully defined.</li> <li>You have experience scaling organisations through periods of rapid growth, organisational change or market expansion.</li> <li>You enjoy solving organisational and business problems, not just technical ones.You can balance strategy and execution, translating ambitious goals into tangible outcomes.</li> <li>You are comfortable making decisions in environments where there is rarely a perfect answer.</li> <li>You have a strong track record of building high-performing leadership teams and developing future leaders.</li> <li>You are energised by the challenge of building something new and helping shape the future of Monzo's international expansion.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>The interview process</strong></h3> <p>After an informal ~30 min recruiter call our interview process involves 2 main stages: </p> <ol> <li><strong>Initial Call (1 hour)</strong> You'll meet with one of our senior engineering leaders. They'll ask you about your previous experience, in particular people leadership, product delivery and technical leadership. They’ll ask example based questions (‘Tell me about a time when…’)</li> <li><strong>Loop Stage</strong> - This is one stage with 4 interviews (totalling 4 hours) split between a collaboration with one of our engineers on a technical exercise, as well as execution and leadership interviews.</li> </ol> <p>At all stages we’ll create space for you to ask as many questions as you have, you’re interviewing us as well!</p> <p>Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. You will have the chance to speak to our recruitment team at various points during your process but if you do have any specific questions ahead of this please contact us on <a href="mailto:tech-hiring@monzo.com">tech-hiring@monzo.com</a>. Please also use that email to let us know if there's anything we can do to make your application process easier for you, because of disability, neurodiversity or any other personal reason.<br><br></p> <p><strong>How we work 💻:</strong></p> <p><strong>Locations & Flexible Working (If you're in the UK) : </strong></p> <p>Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. </p> <p>We value meeting in person but there’s no pressure to come into the office, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨</p> <p>Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.</p> <p><strong>Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life.</strong></p> <p>At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. </p> <p>You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨</p> <p>Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼</p> <h3><strong>What’s in it for you</strong></h3> <p>✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK or Spain</p> <p>✅ We can sponsor visas for the UK (not Spain)</p> <p>📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).</p> <p>⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.</p> <p>📚Learning budget of £1,000 ( a year for books, training courses and conferences</p> <p>#LI-AL1 #LI-REMOTE</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/diversity-and-inclusion">blog</a>, 2026 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/our-2026-diversity-and-inclusion-report" target="_blank">Diversity and Inclusion Report</a> and 2025 <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/gender-pay-gap-report-2025">Gender Pay Gap Report.</a></p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.</p> <p>If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage 😊</p></div>

title: Senior Software Engineer, Agents
description: RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue. We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading. The Role RevenueCat helps app developers manage subscriptions and make more money from them. Maybe you're an indie developer who doesn’t know what "conversion" even means, you just want your app to make money so you can keep building it. Or maybe you're a growth specialist at a company doing millions a month, and pricing experiments are already your whole job. Either way, you probably didn't get into this to spend your days staring at a dashboard. So we built two AI agents to do that work for you, or make you even sharper at it if you're already a pro. Enter Rico. Rico watches over your subscription business and can help you make sense of it, and act on what it finds. Say your revenue dropped last week. You don't need to go digging through charts to find out why. Just ask Rico. It pulls the data, explains what happened in plain language, and shows you how you compare to similar apps. Then it can fix things itself, like setting up a new plan or restoring a customer's access, with you approving the change before it goes live. Run a pricing experiment and Rico will read the results for you and tell you which version is winning. There are so many things we want Rico to be able to do! Then there's our AI Paywall Editor, a specialized agent to build and edit paywalls, the screen that asks someone to subscribe. Most developers are not designers, and a paywall that actually gets people to tap "subscribe" is harder to build than it looks, so the AI Paywall Editor helps you with that. Use it in our online editor, from the command line, or hook your own AI tools into it over MCP. You can see both agents in action in our most recent product launch recap . This is a role for engineers who've built advanced agents that do actual work , not just a thin wrapper around an LLM. You'll ship agentic features to thousands of developers, and you’ll shape the foundation everything else runs on: orchestration, tool execution, context management, evaluation and human-in-the-loop controls. About You You have 8+ years of experience shipping production systems. You've built agents that other people actually use and the systems around them: tool use, structured output, context management, evaluation, orchestration. You have strong backend fundamentals. You've built systems that need to be reliable, observable, and secure. You hold a high bar for quality and instinctively know which details matter, but also are discerning enough to cut scope when needed while still delivering value. You’re customer-obsessed: you imagine yourself as the developer, product manager, or marketer using the feature or experiencing the issue. You’re a builder, not an implementer: scoping, prioritizing, and driving rollout in partnership with our Product team. This isn’t a role where you check off items from a detailed specification. You can quickly familiarize yourself with code you didn't write yourself and improve it. You’re scrappy and biased toward shipping. You’d rather ship a good version today and iterate than wait to ship a perfect one next quarter. You communicate clearly, both in real-time and asynchronously. We’re a fully remote team, and how you write is as important as how you code. You’ve shipped meaningful user-facing features to production, monitored their usage and adoption, and improved them over time. You write high-quality, well-tested code, debug issues methodically, and help raise the engineering bar through thoughtful feedback and mentorship. You act like an founder:: you notice problems, propose improvements, and follow through fast. You're comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early stage product inside a growth stage company, and the architecture is still being figured out. You're self directed. You figure out what needs to be built, build it, and ship it. You are curious and stay current on AI tools and practices. You have a habit of sharing what you learn with others. Ideally, you have: Familiarity with subscription business models, app stores, or developer tools Experience with OpenAI/Anthropic APIs specifically Experience with observability frameworks (Langfuse, Langchain, etc.) Built Slack integrations Contributed to open source AI/ML tooling Maintained systems at scale In the first month, you’ll: Meet frequently with your team and manager to get up to speed Learn our tools, processes, and the subscription business concepts that shape our product Get familiar with our debugging tools, infrastructure, and overall architecture Ship your first project: a small feature that gets you into the codebase and shows you how the agents talk to RevenueCat's APIs Jump in early: fix bugs, ship small improvements, and weigh in on PRs Within the first 3 months, you’ll: Ship a medium sized project, ideally a new agentic feature that reaches tens of thousands of developers Understand the main product areas your team owns and how they work end to end Understand our current agent infrastructure, orchestration, the eval pipeline, the tool framework, and the trust and permissions layer, and have opinions on how to improve it Scope and work on projects on your own, from idea to post launch improvements Take part in code reviews, bug bashes, and technical discussions Within the first 6 months, you’ll: Become the go to engineer for certain focus areas Have made the agents measurably more reliable, faster, and capable Contribute to architecture discussions that affect more than just your team Mentor other engineers joining the team Talk directly with customers to understand how your work actually lands Debug issues across frontend, backend, and data. Communicate clearly during incidents and drive fixes that prevent repeats Learn the basics of incident response and join the on call rotation Within the first 12 months, you’ll: Have built infrastructure the rest of the team ships agents on top of Know all the major components of our system and be able to debug complex issues Write proposals and drive major architecture discussions Spec and architect large projects, gather feedback, and drive design validation and rollout plans Have made RevenueCat an AI native company in large part because you built the engine underneath it Have your own initiatives for improving our product and systems, grounded in real customer priorities What we offer: Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator 10-year window to exercise vested equity options A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually Paid desk at a co-working space Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend Interviewing at RevenueCat Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat , including tips to help you succeed. More on how we work: How we think about hiring and team design: Building a Winning Team The values that guide how we work: Our Values How we work as a remote team: How We Work Remotely at RevenueCat What to expect from our interview process: Interview Expectations What to expect from comp and employment: Employment FAQ
